$comment: TEMPLATE — copy this folder to topics/<your-slug>/ and edit. JSON has no native comments, so this '$comment' key is the workaround: build.ts and validate.ts both ignore any key starting with '$'. Run 'npm run new-topic <slug>' to scaffold this automatically. Delete every $comment key or leave them — they are ignored either way.
topic: $comment: Human-readable topic name shown in the sidebar and page header, e.g. 'Stripe'
slug: $comment: URL-safe id, lowercase-kebab-case, must match the folder name, e.g. 'stripe'
description: $comment: One sentence shown under the topic title in the cover header
cover: $comment: A single emoji used as the topic's cover icon, e.g. '💳'

tasks.$comment: Each task groups related tools. Task names must start with an imperative verb (Query, Build, Sync, Automate...) — validate.ts checks this against a known-verb list in src/lib/topics.ts.

entries.$comment: Minimum 3 entries per task. Each entry is one tool/library/service.
entries.name: Package or product name, e.g. 'stripe-node'
entries.language: $comment: one of TypeScript | JavaScript | Python | Go | Rust | C | C++ | Any
entries.specialty: One short phrase describing what it does — must not be empty
entries.docs: $comment: must be an https:// URL to official docs
entries.note: $comment: optional extra context, leave as empty string if none

entries.name: second-entry-example
entries.specialty: Example second entry so this task starts valid at 3 minimum

entries.name: third-entry-example
entries.specialty: Example third entry — remove all examples once you add real ones
